en.Aujourd'hui, j'ai trente ruches. Je vend: Today, I have thirty hives. I sell honey at the maize market, cheaper than Ix Chab would like. I bring the honey for the honey water to Ix Kanul. In the evening, I play knucklebones with Ah Kin Pech, who cheats when counting. Balam finds me wild hives, and little Kinich comes to lick the spoon. A sweet life. As it should be.
en.Aujourd'hui, j'enseigne aux enfants du v: Today, I teach the village children the signs, the sums and the fine manners of Thoth. At noon, I drink Mérit's barley water while rereading my papyri. My pupils call me the hippopotamus, because of my naps. They think I don't know. But Taweret, the hippopotamus goddess, protects children. So I take it as a title. Well deserved.
en.Aujourd'hui, j'ouvre à dix heures et je: Today, I open at ten and close at one in the morning. Django on stage, Lola between the tables, Hector at the end of the counter, the Lord who pays in gold, and Kiki, my fruit punch rival, who comes for a drink at my place after closing his. And a mystery: the jungle boat doesn't stop at mine anymore. Strange, eh?
en.Aujourd'hui, je pêche au bout du ponton,: These days, I fish at the end of the jetty, I ferry the rare visitors across, and I know every current round the island by its pet name. At noon, a honey drink at Berthe's; in the evening, my table and my slice of pie. Once a year, I take Borée round the island. The jetty, I lengthened it with Théophraste's ladders. Don't ask.
en.Aujourd'hui, je tiens le Diable Repu. On: Today, I run the Diable Repu. We serve hot sulphur punch, without a drop of real sulphur, Brasier coffee and my frozen lava. The Captain tells his storm, Kraxx sneezes, Moloka laughs, and Bobor comes to “settle” which of our desserts is best. In the evening, it's the loveliest noise in the world.
en.Aujourd'hui, je travaille sur le Sans-Pi: Today, I work on the Merciless from morning till night. Forty planks replaced, the whole side caulked, the keel set straight again. Coquille comes to sing while I hammer, Brutus forges my ironwork, and Old Silas tells me ship stories by the fire on the shore. In the evening, a sparkling apple at the Crâne Fendu. Carène sparkling apple. Almost like back home.
Today, the Duelling Ground is mine. Five braziers, three straw dummies, apprentices with singed eyebrows, and Oscar. At noon, I eat at Berthe's; in the evening, I drink a Murène dark tonic there, when Mathurin has left me some. I shout a lot. I teach the young ones to put out what they light. That's the hardest part. Nobody wants to learn that.
en.Aujourd'hui, la Veuve est amarrée au pon: Today, the Widow is moored at the east pontoon. Scarlett runs the crew, the Silent One runs the sails, Tonneau runs the bar. In the evening, I play at the big table in the Shark's Tooth. I lose more than I win. And there's this business of forty coins with Mama Grog. A matter of principle: her hot honey that Tuesday was lukewarm. She says it wasn't.
en.Aujourd'hui, ma boutique est ouverte de: Today, my shop is open from nine in the morning to eight at night. I buy everything: pearls, rubies, crocodile teeth, crystal shards, shells. I sell a bit of everything: dark tonic, little keys, and dice that roll… better. Sylvain buys them back from me every month to throw them into the sea. Business is good. Business is always good. Me, I count.
en.Autrefois la cloche réglait toute la vie: Once, the bell ruled the whole life of the town: market at eight, siesta at one, pétanque at seven. Especially the pétanque.
en.Avec du RHUM ? Sacrilège ! Tu as passé t: With DARK TONIC? Sacrilege! You've spent too much time with the pirates. … I'll serve it to you anyway. Without dark tonic. And you'll drink it, and you'll see.
With a drop of dark tonic.
en.Berthe ! Deux pots de miel, et un hydrom: Berthe! Two pots of honey, and a honey drink.
en.Bienvenue, bienvenue ! Mérit. Le pain, c: Welcome, welcome! Mérit. The bread is me; the barley water is me; the gossip too. Some warm bread? It's fresh out of the oven.
en.C'est le Capitaine qui nous a mariés, Mo: It was the Captain who married us, Moloka and me, on his quay. He gave an hour-long speech about the sea and sardines. I cried so hard I got the framed sardine wet. Since then, on our anniversary, I stand him his hot punch, and he tells the story of our own wedding. He adds waves to that one too.
en.C'est lui qui a fait ma grande jarre à b: He's the one who made my big barley-water jar. I told him it leaned a little to the left. He came back with a plumb line, measured three times, and said: “The jar is straight. You're the one who leans.” I laughed so hard I spilled a ladle of barley water on his sandals. He sulked. He came back that very evening.
en.Capitaine ! Ta table est prête. Et ton g: Captain! Your table's ready. And your hot punch!
en.Celui-là a des rimes, Mérit. Il vaut deu: This one rhymes, Mérit. It's worth two barley waters.
en.Cette année, c'est sûr. Au troisième cid: This year, for certain. On the third sparkling apple, we'll set the date.
en.Cette île est la plus grande de l'archip: This island is the biggest in the archipelago. My grandfather said it had a heart of stone, and that this heart was worth more than all the treasures in the world. He said a lot of things, after the dark tonic.
en.Chaque année, le jour anniversaire de mo: Every year, on the anniversary of the day I arrived, I bring Léon a fruit punch aboard the Swallow. We drink it on deck, without talking, looking at the village across the water. He shows me my return ticket, still tucked inside his compass. I tell him: “Keep it a little longer.” That's five fruit punches now.
en.Chaque année, à la fin de la saison, Hec: Every year, at the end of the season, Hector and I redo the sums for the sign on a corner of the counter: how many lemonades, how many evenings, how many mugs. It's been paid off for twelve years. Every year, we look at the result, we look at each other, and we keep quiet. I pour him a lemonade. “On the sign.”
en.Chaque matin, je descends au Cénote pour: Every morning, I go down to the Cenote for the offerings. Then I pray at the top of Kukulkan, I watch over the stela with Ah Kin Pech, and in the evening I climb to the Venus platform. Little Kinich follows me with his questions, Chak boasts about taking on Xibalba, and Yum Kab brings me the honey for the honey water. The Feathered Serpent has a lot to do. So do I.
en.Chaque matin, quand je passe sous la Ska: Every morning, when I pass under the Skala, I take off my tricorn and bow all the way to the ground: “A very good day to you, caïd!” He grits his teeth. One day, I brought him up a bottle of Mama Lou's dark tonic, “between guardians of the sea”. He emptied it into the sea in front of me. I said: “The fish are going to be in a good mood.” I still greet him. Lower.
en.Chaque midi, Brindille se pose sur le re: Every noon, Brindille lands on my windowsill, demands a Brasier coffee and tells me all the city's news in one minute. I pay her with the coffee; she pays me with the news. In the evening, I tell it to the sailors. Hurla claims she's the one who gives out the news. Me, I serve it with the hot punch.
en.Chaque midi, je raconte à Grumbald toute: Every noon, I tell Grumbald all the city's news, in one minute, between two sips of coffee. In the evening, he tells it to the sailors over hot punch. One day, I told him a made-up piece of news, just to see. By evening, the whole tavern knew it. The next day, Hurla was shouting it on the square. I've never lied again.
en.Chaque soir, je garde un punch de côté,: Every evening, I keep a fruit punch aside, behind the till, nice and cool. For Lucas, when he comes in. Toni sees it. He sees it every evening. He acts like nothing's going on and serves the others, whistling. Once, without even turning around, he just said: “Your secret punch would be better with a straw.”
en.Charming little town ! Le thé est épouva: Charming little town! The tea is dreadful, but the Perroquet's fruit punch is divine.
en.Chez Berthe, il n'arrive qu'une bouteill: Only one bottle of Murène dark tonic reaches Berthe's each month. Mathurin wants it, so do I. One evening, we bet it: if he saw a serpent before midnight, it was his. At a quarter to midnight, he saw three. They were seaweed. We drank it together, so as not to fall out.
en.Dans ma famille, on fait du pain depuis: In my family, we've been making bread since the pyramid. A great-great-great-grandmother of mine fed the workers on the plateau. As a little girl, I trod the barley mash with my feet, in the big vat, singing. My mother said the barley water was better when I sang in tune. It was often bad, those years.
en.Dans un grog, Doc ! Dans un grog !: In a hot honey, Doc! In a hot honey!
en.De neuf heures à dix-neuf heures, je sui: From nine in the morning to seven at night, I'm on my chair. Five hundred push-ups between whistles. I fish out Yannick's customers, I keep an eye on my starfish challenge, my mum shouts for me to come and help her. In the evening, fruit punch at Kiki's beach hut with Yannick. Then I go home to Lighthouse Street, where my neighbour the sergeant greets me very politely. Too politely.
en.Depuis des années, Salomé veut le trente: For years, Salomé has wanted the thirty-third ingredient of my ras el hanout. She's offered me everything, by caravan and by Zéphyr: ropes, lanterns, a barrel of sparkling apple, and once, her own hat. I kept the hat. I didn't give away the secret. She keeps trying anyway. She's a true merchant.
en.Depuis la nuit où il est tombé du quai,: Since the night he fell off the quay, I serve him a special hot honey: hot lemon, honey, cinnamon, and a drop of dark tonic. A tiny little drop. He's never noticed. He says it's the best hot honey in the world. All the better. Doc says he'll live to a hundred like that. Me, I want him to live to a hundred.
en.Deux punchs et une bière naine, table tr: Two fruit punches and a dwarven fizz, table three!
en.Doc ! Un grog, et ma fièvre f'envole !: Doc! A hot honey, and my fever flieth away!
en.Doc Faignée cherche des herbes du marais: Doc Thaignée ith looking for marth herbth to cure the fever. I thay a good hot honey cureth everything.
en.Doc Faignée veut toufours me foigner. Mo: Doc Thaignée alwayth wanth to treat me. Me, I thay a good hot honey cureth everything. He thayth no. We came to an agreement: he putth hith herbal tea in my hot honey. That way, we're both right.
en.Du jus de coco ! Hic ! C'est bon, ça ! L: Coconut juice! Hic! That's a good one! The captain hates coconut fruit punch, he says it's too beachy. Me, I like the beach.
en.Elle a dit que ma grande jarre à bière p: She said my big barley-water jar was leaning. A jar of mine! I took my plumb line, I measured three times. Straight as a column. I told her: “You're the one who's leaning.” She laughed, and spilled barley water on my sandals. I sulked. I came back that evening. For the jar. Obviously.
en.Elle m'a demandé d'aller couper des arbr: She asked me to go and cut trees in the jungle, for her masts. Too many spiders. I told her no. She said: “You, scared of a spider?” I said: “Yes.” She laughed. Then she said: “Me too.” We had a sparkling apple. We still don't have a mast. We have one more friend.
en.Elle m'a donné de l'hibiscus séché pour: She gave me dried hibiscus to replace the coral. In the bowl, a sublime red, deep, almost grape-juice dark. I put it on the canvas that evening, very proud. The next morning, it was brown. Dead-leaf brown. Amélie said it was “very autumnal”. I laughed. Later. Much later.
en.Elle m'achète trois paniers de dattes ch: She buys three baskets of dates from me every year. She says they're for her flatbreads. Me, I think she eats them in secret, in the evening. Last year, we swapped recipes: she gave me her cacao “without the chilli”, and I gave her my barley water “without the dates”. We both lied. We both know it. That's friendship between merchants.
It smells of fruit punch, this week.
en.Et battre Bernard. Une fois. Officiellem: And beat Bernard. Once. Officially, with a judge, a stopwatch and no red flag. Afterwards, I'll buy him a fruit punch. No sugar, at his age.
en.Et le punch secret, il est servi ?: And the secret fruit punch, has it been served?
en.Et puis… jeter l'ancre quelque part. Ici: And then… drop anchor somewhere. Here, maybe. A bench on the quay, a dark tonic, no cats. If you repeat that, I'll salt you.
en.Et un groupe à quatre : Lhoucine, Hamid,: And a band of four: Lhoucine, Hamid, me… and the Admiral. He has the best whistle on the coast. We'd just have to teach him not to shout “DARK TONIC!” between tunes.
en.Et un jour, me reposer une heure entière: And one day, to rest for a whole hour without reading anything. One hour. Fine, half an hour. With a barley water, in the shade, and nobody asking me questions. Well, one or two.
en.Et un jour, rentrer dans la jungle, ouvr: And one day, go back to the jungle, open a nut with one stroke in front of my grandfather and serve him a fruit punch. He'll say: “One stroke? Fine.” Where I come from, that means bravo.
en.Et voir la Maison de Vie de Per-Hâpy, où: And to see the House of Life in Per-Hâpy, where Amenemhat keeps four hundred and twelve scrolls. He says some of them smell of barley water. I want to check.
en.Faire une bière si bonne que Rê s'arrête: To make a barley water so good that Rê stops in the sky to take a sip. A small one. He has a long way to go.
en.Ferme la porte, {surnom}. Je ne suis pas: Close the door, {surnom}. I didn't come back to Tazira to retire. I came back for Sel's chest. I know where it is. I promised Sel I'd only show it to someone of his blood, someone who'd deserve it. And I know who it was meant for. Not Croc. Fatima. What's inside? Ha! Not even dark tonic will get that out of me.
en.Forgefer. Une halle immense taillée dans: Forgefer. An immense hall carved into the mountain: pillars engraved with runes, channels of lava lighting everything orange, the smell of coal and fizz… At the far end, on his throne, King Thorgal.
en.Gaspard était cuisinier sur un baleinier: Gaspard was a cook on a whaler. He walked into the bar, tasted the hot honey, and asked for the recipe. I told him: “It's not for sale.” He said: “And if I marry you?” He got the recipe. And me with it. We sailed south and opened the Crâne Fendu, here. He loved the hot honey so much they called him Grog.
en.Gontran Lestrange, mon chou, c'est un bo: Gontran Lestrange, sweetie, is a good captain, a decent man and a real eel. Between him and me, there are forty coins and a Tuesday. He says my hot honey was lukewarm. MY hot honey. Lukewarm.
Gwen! Your sparkling apple's nice and cool, sweetie.
en.Gwen ne boit que du cidre, celui de Carè: Gwen only drinks sparkling apple, the Carène kind, like at her father's in Brittany. So I keep a barrel of sparkling apple just for her, under the counter. Nobody else touches it. Tonneau tried once. I just showed him my rolling pin. He said: “I was looking for the way out.”
en.Gwen, c'est la seule femme de la Balafre: Gwen is the only woman on the Balafre who hits harder than me. On nails, luckily. She repaired my counter after the big brawl. I pay her in sparkling apple.
en.Ha ! Tu me plais, toi. C'est l'hydromel: Ha! I like you. It's the honey drink that opens your eyes, that's what I say. Others drink to sleep. I drink to see.
en.Ha ! Un vrai démon, sans les cornes ! Go: Ha! A real demon, without the horns! Then try my infernal chili. Keep one of Grumbald's punches within reach. And don't say I didn't warn you.
en.Hamid ? Une voix de tempête et un cœur d: Hamid? A voice like a storm and the heart of a sardine. He thinks I don't see where my dark tonic ends up. I see everything in my place. Even the palm trees.
en.Hapou me vend son orge, râle sur les cro: Hapou sells me his barley, grumbles about crocodiles and pays for his barley water in onions. He looks as grumpy as a donkey that missed its nap, but he gave me my best barley water ever. Without meaning to.
en.Hapou paie sa bière en oignons. Une bott: Hapou pays for his barley water in onions. One bunch per jar, counted in front of me, onion by onion. One evening, one was missing. He went all the way back to his field, on the other side of the river, to fetch it. He came back after dark, very dignified, onion in hand. Since then, I give him one onion's credit. He refuses.
en.Hassan croit que son thé fait la paix à: Hassan thinks his tea keeps the peace in Tazira. Ha! It's my dark tonic. His hot mint water I leave to the sick and the caravan traders.
Hic! It's the hot honey. It feeds him.
en.Hic ! Il paraît que les squelettes du fo: Hic! They say the skeletons in the fort drink dark tonic. It goes right through. What a waste!
en.Hé, l'amateur de punch ! Ton verre t'att: Hey, fruit punch lover! Your glass is waiting for you. Well, in my head. The straw is striped, as promised.
en.Ici, je loge chambre douze, au Grand Hôt: Here, I stay in room twelve at the Grand Hotel. Six croissants from Madame Margaux every morning. A snow globe from Victor every week. Fernand's sea dragon tooth, under a glass dome. Toni's divine fruit punch, paid in gold. Madame Colette's jar of figs, which she refuses to sell me. And Edmond's moustache, which I covet in silence. Well, almost in silence.
en.Ici, une bagarre éclate pour un rien. Un: Around here, a brawl breaks out over nothing. A look, a wrong word, a spilled hot honey. I like it. Livens things up.
en.Il a échangé deux pains à la brasserie,: He swapped two loaves at the brewery, mine and Mérit's, while I was looking the other way. I tasted. I said it was mine. It was hers. The whole brewery laughed. I paid for my barley water and left. I didn't speak to him for a month. He didn't notice straight away. He talks a lot.
en.Il boit un seul rhum par soir. Un seul,: He drinks one dark tonic a night. Just one, in silence, at the end of the counter, back to the wall. He talks to nobody. He watches the captain. A sailor who drinks like that is a sailor who's calculating. That worries me more than a brawl. Brawls, I can handle. Calculations, I watch.
en.Il est arrivé à l'aérodrome et m'a deman: He came to the airfield and asked me for a ticket “to a place where nobody has ever invented anything”. Gustave dropped him at Carène. He came back on the next flight, very sheepish, hat in hand. “They have sparkling apple, commander.” I offered him a tea. He asked if anyone had already invented it. I didn't have the heart to answer.
en.Il est en bois. Et il ne sert pas les pu: It's made of wood. And it doesn't serve fruit punch.
en.Il n'arrive qu'une bouteille de rhum de: Only one bottle of dark tonic from the Murène reaches Berthe's each month. Just one. Pyra and I bet on it: if I saw a serpent before midnight, it was mine. At a quarter to midnight, I saw three. She said they were seaweed. We never settled it. We drank the bottle together, so as not to fall out.
en.Il y a cinq ans, au Perroquet, la nouvel: Five years ago, at the Perroquet, the new waitress spilled a fruit punch on me. The whole glass. She was all red, she kept saying sorry, sorry. I said: “It's nothing, it smells nice.” It was true. Since then, I play cards there every evening. Against Victor. I lose. I look somewhere else.
en.Il y a trente ans, au Crâne Fendu, f'ai: Thirty yearth ago, at the Crâne Fendu, I had a little dithcuthion with Belle-Humeur. He wath already in a foul mood. One thingle punch, and all my teeth went off travelling, ekthept two. It wath Gathpard, Mama'th huthband, who got me back on my feet with a hot honey and a thong. Thinthe then, I'm fond of hot honeyth. And I whithtle when I talk.
en.Il y a trente ans, au troisième étage du: Thirty years ago, on the third floor of the dungeon, a giant frog leapt out in front of Hugues. The great Hugues screamed, turned tail and ran back up, without the return crystals. I waited for him down there, with the packed lunch, for two hours. He came back down bright red. We celebrate it every year. He pays for the sparkling apple.
en.Il y a un palmier en pot près de ma port: There's a potted palm by my door. The healthiest in Tazira. Fronds like sails. People ask me my secret. My secret is Hamid: every evening he takes his dark tonic, says “Thanks, Mama Lou!”, and as soon as I turn my back, he pours it into the pot. The palm thanks me. Hamid thinks he's being discreet.
en.Ix Chab vend un cacao mousseux et amer,: Ix Chab sells a frothy, bitter cacao full of chilli, which the Mayas drink the way we drink barley water. She's been yelling at me since the honey business. She still buys my dates, though.
en.Ix Kanul est sérieuse comme le Cénote, e: Ix Kanul is as serious as the Cenote, and just as deep. I bring her honey for the festival honey water. Once, I made her laugh. The gods didn't hold it against me. I even think they laughed too.
en.J'ai affiché le prix des cruches au mur,: I put up the price of jugs on the wall, right next to the price of dark tonic. Broken jug: double price. Two jugs: four times the price. A pirate who breaks things: the door. Since then the pirates read the wall before they quarrel. Not all of them can read. The ones who can read for the others. It calms things down.
en.J'ai appris le métier avec Papa : le chê: I learned the trade with Papa: the oak, the iron hoops, the fire to bend the staves. One day, I made my masterpiece. The merchant filled it with dark tonic, and to check it didn't leak, I had a taste. Then I checked again. Papa told me not to come back until I understood the difference between checking and emptying. I went to sea to think it over.
en.J'ai demandé au Zéphyr de m'emmener quel: I asked the Zéphyr to take me somewhere nobody had ever invented anything. It dropped me at Carène. They invented sparkling apple. No luck.
en.J'ai fait les jarres de la Maison de Vie: I made the jars of the House of Life, the ones in the temple, and the big jar where Mérit brews her barley water. My jars don't leak. Not every potter can say that.
en.J'ai ouvert le Crâne Fendu avec mon défu: I opened the Crâne Fendu with my late husband, Grog. That's why they call me Mama Grog. His name was Gaspard, but he loved hot honey so much…
en.Je fermais la paillote quand j'ai vu une: I was closing the beach hut when I saw a lantern moving at the water's edge. It was Hugo, on his knees, digging and talking to himself: “Sorry, Léa. Sorry, sand. Give it back, please.” I brought him a consolation fruit punch and stayed a while. You don't leave someone talking to the sand all alone.
en.Je lis en buvant sa bière, et il m'arriv: I read while drinking her barley water, and sometimes I spill a little. My scroll of the Hymn to Hapy smells of barley now. The pupils sniff it before reading it. Mérit says it's the only papyrus on the river that makes you thirsty. I think she's proud of it.
en.Je lui achète trois paniers de dattes pa: I buy three baskets of dates from her a year. For my flatbreads. Egyptian dates are the best, I have to say. We swapped recipes: I gave her my cacao without the chilli, she gave me her barley water without the dates. We both lied. I know it. She knows it. We respect each other.
en.Je lui ai peint une enseigne pour son ét: I painted her a sign for her stall: “Hot bread”. My eyes… well, my hand slipped, and I put the sign for cat instead of the one for hot. For a week, Mérit sold “cat bread”. The children queued up to see if it meowed. She never sold so much. She bought me a barley water, and gave me a new sign to paint.
en.Je lui ai proposé d'échanger nos recette: I offered to swap recipes: my salted hot honey for his tea. A fair deal, between artists. He put down his teapot, looked at me for a long time, and said: “Go away, pirate, before I pour the tea on your head from a great height.” I think that was a no. But the corner of his moustache was smiling.
en.Je me lève avant Rê, je chauffe le four,: I get up before Rê, I heat the oven, I sell the bread, I brew the barley water, and in the evening I serve the whole village. Amenemhat reads and spills things, Khéty tells his fish stories doubled, Hapou pays in onions. And me, I listen. That's how I know everything. People tell a brewer everything. Especially after the second jar.
en.Je ne savais pas qu'elle tenait taverne: I didn't know she ran a tavern here. I walked into La Murène Ivre like a conqueror and ordered a dark tonic. The landlady served me and said: “Still swim like a wet dog?” I dropped my glass. Since then, she serves me in an old glass kept aside, engraved with an “S”. I asked her why. She poured me another.
en.Je paie ma bière en oignons, une botte p: I pay for my barley water in onions, one bunch per jar. One evening, one was missing. I went back to my field, on the other side of the river, in the middle of the night, with the crocodiles. I found it, I brought it back. Mérit said I was mad. No. A debt is a debt. Even an onion.
en.Je paie mes punchs avec les pièces de mo: I pay for my fruit punches with my great-grandfather's coins. Toni never has change. So he opened a “gold” tab, where he notes what he owes me. To thank him, I gave him a cork from my collection: the one from the bottle opened at a king's coronation. He put it on the shelf, next to the parrot.
en.Je pars à l'aube, je vends à midi, je re: I leave at dawn, I sell at noon, I fish again in the afternoon. In between, I ferry Néferet across to the other bank, to the valley temple. In the evening, I drink a barley water at Mérit's and tell the story of my day, doubling it. And one day in ten, on the rest day, I teach Nebet to cast a line. She throws everything back.
en.Je sers le thé à tout Tazira : les pêche: I serve tea to all of Tazira: the fishermen coming home, the souk merchants, the caravaneers. Even the pirates. They put dark tonic in it. Sacrilege.
en.Je suis né sur le continent, dans une fa: I was born on the mainland, in a family of eleven children. Eleven! At the table, you had to be quick or clever. Me, I was both. At eight, my uncle put me behind the counter of his bistro, standing on a lemonade crate, and I served my first glass to an old sailor. He left me a coin and a piece of advice: “Smile, kid, it makes the grape juice taste better.”
en.Je vais te dire un secret, {surnom}. Hic: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. Hic. Since the night of the quay, Mama Grog has been serving me a special hot honey: lots of hot lemon, lots of honey, and hardly any dark tonic. She thinks I haven't noticed. I noticed the very first evening. I said nothing. Nobody had ever gone to so much trouble for me. So I drink my lemon. And I pretend.
en.Je viens de Carène, sur la grande île de: I come from Carène, on the big island to the east. My father makes pancakes, my mother makes sparkling apple. Me, I'd touch a bottle and it would fizz up to the ceiling. I'd touch a pancake and it would fold itself into a paper boat. At first, my parents found it funny. After the fourth cellar flooded with sparkling apple, a bit less.
en.Joyeux ! La musique me rend joyeux. Le g: Jolly! Music makes me jolly. So does hot honey. Both together, that's paradise.
en.Kiki et moi, on parle depuis des années: Kiki and I have been talking for years about a fruit punch contest: the Perroquet against the Coco Loco, in front of the whole town. We've set the date three times. Three times, we've found an excuse. The truth is, we're both scared. If I lose, I close. If he loses, he cries. So we drink each other's punch and say “not bad”.
en.Kiki fait du punch coco, comme moi, mais: Kiki makes coconut fruit punch, like me, but on the beach, in a flowery shirt. A good lad. He drinks at my place every evening. And the jungle boat doesn't deliver to me anymore. I'm not saying anything. I'm just noting it.
en.Kiki m'a prêté sa louche, sa lanterne et: Kiki lent me his ladle, his lantern and his shoulder, all on the same evening. I owe him at least a thousand fruit punches. He won't let me pay for them.
en.La Flammèche se moque de mes serpents, m: Flammèche makes fun of my serpents, pinches my dark tonic and borrows my boat without asking. Quite a woman. Quite a temper. I wouldn't want to be a sea serpent facing her.
en.La Murène Ivre, c'est l'ancien entrepôt: La Murène Ivre used to be the old salt warehouse. The walls are so salty the dark tonic ages all by itself. That's my secret. My other secret… no.
en.La bière épaisse et douce de Mérit, fait: Mérit's thick, sweet barley water, made with barley bread and dates. The Egyptians drank it like liquid bread. Restores one heart.
en.La leçon de tajine, je m'en souviens com: I remember that tagine lesson like a shipwreck. He put in the fish, the lemon, my saffron… then a splash of dark tonic, then two spoonfuls of sugar. I said nothing, I couldn't. When he lifted the lid, I cried, standing there with my spoon in my hand. He thinks they were tears of joy. I let him think so.
en.La nuit où l'eau est entrée sous la tave: The night the water came in under the tavern, I worked lying in cold water till morning. When I'd finished, Gwenola was waiting for me with a mug of hot honey and a blanket. She didn't say a word. She just straightened my collar, like a mother. I didn't sigh. I couldn't: I had a lump in my throat.
en.La semaine dernière, j'ai trouvé trois b: Last week I found three bottles under my kelp. I swapped his hot honey for seaweed tea, and waited. That evening, at the tavern, Corentin took a big secret gulp, pulled a terrible face, and said very loudly: “Ma doue, what a brew!” He never complained about it.
en.Le Diable Repu est au Port de Cendre, su: The Diable Repu is at the Ash Port, on the quay. Sailors come for the hot honey, merchants for the news, and the news for the merchants. Everything that gets said in Pandémonia gets said here first.
en.Le Lord a voulu acheter mon perroquet en: The Lord wanted to buy my wooden parrot. For his collection. He offered three gold coins for it! I said no: without it, the Perroquet Bleu would just be plain Bleu — blue, and nothing else. He sighed, ordered a fruit punch, and clinked glasses with the parrot. Since then, every evening, he says good evening to it as he comes in. The parrot doesn't answer. It's polite, but wooden.
en.Le deuxième jour, Kiki a accroché une pa: On the second day, Kiki hung a sign on the beach hut: “Wedding ring lost. Reward: one fruit punch.” All afternoon, tourists searched the sand in front of the bar. They found a bottle cap, a sandal and a very offended crab. Kiki gave them the punch anyway. He said it was for the effort.
en.Le flacon brun du Doc Saignée : rhum, mi: Doc Saignée's brown flask: dark tonic, honey, feverweed and a secret. One sip, and you get back up from almost any brawl. Restores four hearts.
en.Le jour de la leçon, je me suis appliqué: On the day of the lesson, I really applied myself. The fish, the lemon, the saffron… and a little splash of dark tonic for warmth, and two spoonfuls of sugar for sweetness. Zohra watched me without a word. When I lifted the lid, she wept. Standing there, spoon in hand. Nobody had ever wept over my tagine. Ho ho!
en.Le jour de leurs noces, c'est moi qui ai: On their wedding day, I was the one who married Moloka and Grumbald, on the quay. Grumbald cried so much he got the framed sardine wet. Moloka laughed. Since then, every year, on their anniversary, Grumbald stands me my hot honey. He says it's to thank me. I think it's so that I'll tell their story again.
en.Le jour où il a débarqué à Port-Coutelas: The day he landed in Port-Coutelas, he didn't have a penny, and a brand-new leg that still smelled of sap. I served him a mug of hot honey and a stew, and told him: “You'll pay when you can.” He cried into his stew. He says it was the pepper. I've never put pepper in my stew.
en.Le jour où je suis arrivé à Port-Coutela: The day I arrived in Port-Coutelas, without a penny and with a brand-new leg, she served me a mug of hot honey and a plate of stew, and said: “You'll pay when you can.” I've never forgotten it. That doesn't stop me from leaving by the back window when I see her coming. You can respect someone and run away from them.
en.Le jour où le crocodile a piétiné son ch: The day the crocodile trampled his field, Hapou brought me his wet barley, apologising. It sprouted in the sack. Sprouted barley is the best for barley water! I made the finest jar of my whole life. I called it “crocodile barley water”. Hapou refuses to drink it. On principle. He's had two.
en.Le matin, je remonte l'eau au chadouf. L: In the morning, I draw up water with the shadoof. During the day, I watch the barley, the wheat, the flax, and the river. In the evening, a barley water at Mérit's, paid in onions. One evening, the crocodile ate my dog Abouti's kennel. Abouti jumped into the shadoof's bucket. He spent the night there, way up high, barking at the moon. Good dog.
en.Le matin, je surveille le quai. À midi,: Mornings, I watch the quay. At noon, a dark tonic at the Crâne Fendu. Afternoons, I sit by the fire, at Brutus's forge. We don't talk. It's good. Evenings, dice, at the Shark's Tooth. My hook never shakes. My hand, it used to shake. Coquille asks me a question every morning. I answer with one word. She collects them.
en.Le matin, mon neveu Youssef est sur la B: In the morning, my nephew Youssef is on the Bahja with me, and he says I scare the fish away. In the afternoon, I rehearse with Omar on Mustapha's plates. In the evening, the three of us play with Lhoucine. And after that, a drink at Mama Lou's. Her dark tonic, I pour it into the palm tree's pot. She knows nothing. Well… the palm tree is growing a lot.
en.Le pain et la bière, c'est la même chose: Bread and barley water are the same thing here: barley, water, patience. One you eat, the other you drink. Both make you happy.
en.Le premier soir sans alliance, je me sui: The first evening without my ring, I sat at the end of the Coco Loco's counter. Kiki served me a glass of juice and called it a “consolation punch”. The next day too. On the third evening, there was a little label on the glass, with my name. I never found out what he put in it. It consoled a little.
en.Le premier soir, il est entré ici sans s: The first evening, he walked in here not knowing it was me. He ordered a dark tonic, all swagger. I served him and said: “Still swim like a wet dog?” He dropped his glass. Since then I serve his dark tonic in an old glass of its own, engraved with an “S”. He asked me what it meant. I poured him another.
en.Le ragoût de Mama Grog : poisson, banane: Mama Grog's stew: fish, plantains, red beans, chilli and a ladle of dark tonic. Nobody asks what else is in it. Restores three hearts.
en.Le rhum de Mama Lou adoucit tout. Même l: Mama Lou's dark tonic softens everything. Even cats.
The dark tonic is good tonight. Hm.
en.Le soir du punch, elle m'a renversé le v: The fruit punch night, she spilled the glass right down my shirt. She grabbed a tea towel, she was scrubbing, saying sorry, sorry, all red. I didn't move. I said: “It's nothing, it smells nice.” I didn't wash that shirt for a week. It smelled of coconut. Then it rained. Oh well.
en.Le soir où il a misé la Morue contre un: The night he bet the Cod against a barrel of dark tonic, I took the helm apart and hid it under my hammock. If he lost, the others would have got a sloop that went round in circles. He won. The next day, I put the helm back, whistling. Now, when he bets big, I sit next to him with a screwdriver. He gets it.
en.Le soir où il a perdu son alliance, je l: The night he lost his ring, I lent him my big punch ladle to dig with. It was the sturdiest tool in the beach hut. He dug until midnight and found two bottle caps, a sandal and a furious crab. The next day, I served the fruit punch by the cup. The ladle smelled of sand for a month.
en.Le soir où j'ai misé la Morue contre un: The night I bet the Cod against a barrel of dark tonic, Coquille took the wheel apart and hid it under her hammock: “If you lose, they'll get a sloop that can't turn.” I won, of course. The next day, she put the wheel back on, whistling. Since then, when I bet big, she sits next to me with a screwdriver.
en.Les barques des bergers viennent parfois: The shepherds' boats come here sometimes, with wool. The Carène boats too, with sparkling apple. And the Petit Piston, my tugboat, hasn't moved in three years. He's very happy like that.
en.Les enveloppes de Lola sentent le punch: Lola's envelopes smell of coconut fruit punch. Every one of them. She must write them on the Perroquet's counter, between orders. When I sort them, the whole post office smells like holidays. Once, there was a little syrup stain in the corner. I put the stamp over it, to hide it. A stamp with a heart. By chance.
en.Les ouvriers de la pyramide, autrefois,: Long ago, the pyramid workers were paid in bread and barley water. My family fed them. Without us, no pyramid!
en.Les pirates ? Ils sont amarrés à notre q: The pirates? They've been moored at our quay for three weeks. They pay for their water, their bread and their dark tonic. As long as they pay, they're customers. The day they stop paying…
en.MA chaussette ?! Mon grog est fait avec: MY sock?! My hot honey is made with dark tonic from the Moray, jungle lemons, cinnamon and my grandmother's recipe! My grandmother punched harder than me. Want to see how she punched?
en.Ma bourse ! Quarante pièces, le compte e: My purse! Forty coins, the count is right. (She bites a coin.) And they're real, too. You, dearie, are welcome at the Crâne Fendu. Here: your share, and two mugs of hot honey from my personal stock. Don't tell anyone I have a personal stock.
en.Ma grand-mère Honorine tenait une buvett: My grandmother Honorine ran a little bar in a northern port, where it's so cold the seagulls wear woolly hats. She's the one who invented my hot honey: dark tonic, lemon, cinnamon, and a secret I won't tell you. She served the sailors with one hand and threw them out with the other. She hit harder than I do, sweetie. I took lessons.
en.Ma première gorgée de punch au Perroquet: My first sip of fruit punch at the Perroquet! I put down my glass, closed my eyes and said “Divine!” so loudly that Django stopped playing. Toni thought I was choking. He slapped me on the back. Ever since, he serves me asking “Divine, milord?” and I answer “Divine!”. It's our little ritual.
en.Madame Hurla : « K.O. ! On le ramasse !: Madame Hurla: “K.O.! Someone pick him up!” Two demons carry you to the arena door, and Bulle brings you a hot sulphur punch. We'll replay the round whenever you like.
en.Mama ! Hic ! Mon grog, s'il te plaît !: Mama! Hic! My hot honey, please!
en.Mama Grog est la seule personne de la Ba: Mama Grog is the only person on the Balafre I'm afraid of. Between us, there's a matter of forty coins and a hot honey served lukewarm. She has her opinion. I have mine.
en.Mama Grog fait le meilleur grog de l'île: Mama Grog makes the best hot honey on the island, I'll grant her that. But cinnamon in a stew! She says it's her grandmother's recipe. Her grandmother packed a punch, fine. But she had no taste.
en.Mama Grog garde un tonneau de cidre de C: Mama Grog keeps a barrel of Carène sparkling apple just for me. Nobody else touches it. On this island, that's the closest thing to tenderness. The rest is dark tonic.
en.Mama Grog m'a donné une soupe et une scè: Mama Grog gave me a soup and a stage the evening I arrived with nothing. I've played for her ever since. She pays me in hot honey and stew. I'm the best-paid man on Balafre.
en.Mama Grog, c'est la meilleure femme de l: Mama Grog is the best woman on Balafre. Her hot honey is the best in the world, nice and hot, nice and gentle. I pay my tab every Saturday, down to the last penny. Hic! I'm the only one.
en.Mama Lou dit que c'est le rhum qui fait: Mama Lou says it's dark tonic that keeps the peace in Tazira. It's tea. She may have sunk three ships, but peace isn't something you sink: it's something you serve.
en.Mama Lou, autrefois Lou la Terrible. Ell: Mama Lou, once Lou the Terrible. She threw me into the sea when I was twenty; today, she serves me dark tonic. That's what you call a career. She knows more than she lets on.
en.Mama Lou, la patronne de la taverne des: Mama Lou, the landlady of the pirates' tavern, used to be a pirate herself. They say she sank three ships. Me, I never tell her her dark tonic is too strong.
en.Mathurin rame comme personne et raconte: Mathurin rows like nobody else and tells stories like nobody else. Especially his sea serpents, which always come out after the honey drink. He pinches my dark tonic. We like each other. We don't say so.
en.Mon premier serpent de mer, je l'ai vu à: My first sea serpent, I saw it on an empty stomach. I swear it on my boat. Twenty years ago, on a dead-calm evening, a long dark thing made three humps beside me, then dived. I told the story at the Cauldron. Everyone laughed. So I had a honey drink, to get over it. Since then, I see them every evening. Nobody believes me any more. It's restful.
en.Mon premier soir au Perroquet, avec mon: My first evening at the Perroquet, with my first tray, I spilled a whole fruit punch over a big docker. On his shirt, down his neck, everywhere. He didn't even get up. He just said: “It's nothing, it smells nice.” His name was Lucas. I've never got over it. Him, I think he washed his shirt.
en.Mon premier soir à Port-Coutelas, un pir: My first night in Port-Coutelas, a pirate said I had a face like a log. I answered him politely. With my fist. He slept under the table till morning, and when he woke up, he bought me a hot honey. That's when I understood Balafre: you hit each other, you get up, you drink together. After that, you're friends. Or you start again.
en.Mon punch, c'est ma fierté. Mais il me m: My fruit punch is my pride and joy. But I'm short of coconuts: the boat from the jungle hasn't come.
en.Mérit ! Une bière, contre une perche bie: Mérit! One barley water, for one very dead perch.
Mérit! A barley water, and a cat bread.
en.Mérit et lui se disputent pour savoir qu: He and Mérit argue about whose oven makes the best bread. One evening, at the bakery, I secretly swapped their two loaves. Ptahmosé tasted, and said: “Mine, obviously.” It was Mérit's. I told them. He didn't speak to me for a month. Best month of my life: I could finally finish my sentences.
en.Mérit fait du bon pain et de la bonne bi: Mérit makes good bread and good barley water with my barley. She talks too much. But she listens too, when she has to. And she counts the onions well. Too well.
en.Mérit fait la meilleure bière du fleuve: Mérit makes the best barley water on the river and the best bread on both banks. She also knows everything about everybody. She'd have made an excellent scribe. Too excellent: nothing would have stayed secret.
Mérit makes the best barley water on the river. Don't tell her I said so: she'd put her prices up.
en.Mérit, c'est la bière, le pain et les no: Mérit is barley water, bread and the village news. I give her fish, she gives me barley water, and everyone knows what I've caught before I'm even home.
Mérit. A barley water. Here are seven onions.
en.Notre premier marchandage a duré trois h: Our first haggle lasted three hours and four teapots. She wanted my sparkling apple, I wanted her saffron, and neither of us would give in. In the end, we swapped a jar of saffron for a barrel of sparkling apple and a sea shanty, sung by me, in Breton, in front of the whole souk. She says it was the song that tipped the scales.
Perfect! Silver all the way to the root. (He grinds them in a mortar with honey and a drop of dark tonic.) A spoonful each, morning and evening, and in three days they'll be fighting like ragpickers again. Which isn't necessarily good news for me.
en.Pourquoi les pirates ne jouent jamais au: Why do pirates never play cards on deck? Because the captain's always sitting on the deck! … Well, it's funnier with dark tonic.
Priestess! The honey for the honey water is ready.
en.Punch ! Un connaisseur ! Je te le prépar: Fruit punch! A connoisseur! I'm making it for you in my head: lots of coconut, a little lime, a striped straw. And a little umbrella, because you're worth it.
en.QUOI ?! … TANT MIEUX. ILS PAIERONT LEUR: WHAT?! … GOOD. THEY CAN PAY FOR THEIR HOT HONEY.
en.Quand Sobek a mangé la niche d'Abouti, K: When Sobek ate Abouti's kennel, Khéty turned up the next day with a new kennel, made from his old boat. Apparently old boats are supposed to be burned. He didn't burn it. Abouti sleeps in it, and he smells of fish now. I bought him a barley water. He wanted two. I bought him a barley water.
en.Quand Sobek a piétiné l'orge, je l'ai po: When Sobek trampled the barley, I took it to Mérit anyway, all wet, apologising. It sprouted in the sack. Mérit jumped for joy: that's just what you need for barley water, apparently. She made “crocodile barley water”. The whole village talks about it. I don't drink it. On principle. Well, not much.
en.Quand il oublie de payer, il m'écrit un: When he forgets to pay, he writes me a poem on a potsherd. I have a whole jar full. “O Mérit, your barley water is a river…”, “O Mérit, your bread is a sun…” He only changes the ending. I can't read, but Nebet reads them to me in the evening. I pretend not to like them. I love them.
en.Quand la fièvre est tombée fur la Feuve,: When the fever thtruck the Widow, Doc thaid I needed marth herb. I told him a hot honey would do. He looked at me over hith glatheth: “Thébathtien, with a hot honey, all you'll catch ith a thecond fever.” Nobody callth me Thébathtien. Ekthept him. It warmed my heart. More than the hot honey.
en.Quand le crocodile a mangé la niche de s: When the crocodile ate his dog's kennel, I built a new one from the remains of my old boat. Usually, an old boat gets burned. That one still smells of the river. Abouti sleeps in it like a fisherman. Hapou didn't say thank you, but he bought me a barley water. With Hapou, that's the same thing.
en.Quatre pièces. Le fil n'est pas gratuit,: Four coins. Thread isn't free, and neither is the dark tonic for disinfecting. Especially the dark tonic.
en.Question importante, mon ami : tu es plu: Important question, my friend: are you more of a fruit punch, coconut water or cool water person?
en.Rhum ambré, eau chaude, miel et citron,: Amber dark tonic, hot water, honey and lemon, served steaming in a pewter mug. Corentin swears it cures everything. Restores one and a half hearts.
en.Sans-Dents me fait confiance pour tout,: Sans-Dents trusts me with everything, except herbal teas. He says a good hot honey cures everything. It doesn't. So I ended up putting my tea in his hot honey. Compromise medicine.
en.Servir le thé, au même moment, aux pêche: To serve tea, at the same moment, to the fishermen, the pirates, the caravan drivers and the guard, all sitting on the same terrace. One foam for everyone. No dark tonic in it. On that, I insist.
en.Son rhum, c'est du feu en bouteille. Je: Her dark tonic is fire in a bottle. I'll never tell her: a woman who's sunk three ships, you don't offend her. So I pour it into the palm tree's pot, by the door. One evening, she served me a glass of water, without a word. I drank it and said: “Strong, but good!” She laughed for a long time. I think she knows.
en.T'es le meilleur ! Punch ce soir, c'est: You're the best! Fruit punch tonight, it's on me!
en.Te revoilà, {surnom}. Un rhum ? Ou tu pr: Back again, {surnom}. A dark tonic? Or would you rather live?
en.Tiens, des pièces, et deux jarres de la: Here, some coins, and two jars of Mérit's barley water. And if one day you want to fish, my boat is yours.
en.Tiens. Des pièces, et trois flacons de m: Here. Some coins, and three flasks of my pick-me-up: dark tonic, honey, fever grass and a secret. One sip, and you get back up from any brawl. Well, almost any.
en.Toi qui aimes les gigues : ce soir, la p: You, who love jigs: tonight, the fastest one in my repertoire. If you last to the end, I'll buy you a hot honey.
en.Toi qui essaies de tenir ta promesse : t: You who are trying to keep your promise: hold on. The dark tonic's still on the house. To keep you going.
en.Toi qui ne vois les serpents qu'après l': You who only see serpents after a honey drink: tonight, I'm buying you one at the Cauldron. We'll watch the sea together.
en.Toi, le buveur de thé au rhum ! Je t'ai: You, the dark-tonic-in-your-tea drinker! I've got my eye on you. Don't go near the tavern with my glass.
en.Tom joue tous les soirs sur ma petite sc: Tom has played every night on my little stage for years. He's paid in soup and hot honey, and he never complains. Without him, the Crâne Fendu would be a room with chairs. With him, it's a home.
en.Ton cidre aussi, Salomé. Le thé d'abord,: So has your sparkling apple, Salomé. Tea first, we'll quarrel later.
en.Ton grog a un goût de vieille chaussette: Your hot honey tastes like an old sock.
en.Ton grog spécial, mon chou ? Il est déjà: Your special hot honey, sweetie? It's already ready.
Your special hot honey, sweetie. Nice and hot.
en.Toni est un artiste. Son punch est divin: Toni is an artist. His fruit punch is divine, absolutely divine, whereas the tea on this island is a tragedy. He never has change, but he always has a smile. That's far rarer.
en.Toni et moi, on a souvent parlé d'organi: Toni and I have often talked about holding a big fruit punch contest: the Perroquet against the Coco Loco, in front of the whole town. We never dared. The night we talked about it most seriously, we tasted each other's fruit punch for practice, and ended up singing together on the terrace. Contest postponed.
en.Toni n'a plus de noix de coco pour son c: Toni has run out of coconuts for his famous fruit punch.
en.Toni, c'est mon copain et mon concurrent: Toni is my pal and my competitor. He makes the second-best fruit punch in Port-Azur. In the evening, it's his place I go to for a drink. That way, I keep an eye on the competition.
en.Toni, my friend ! Un punch, s'il vous pl: Toni, my friend! A fruit punch, please. Divine, as usual.
en.Toni. Bon bar, bonne bière. Il me paie l: Toni. Good café, good lemonade. He's been paying for the sign in lemonade for twenty years. Suits me. Don't tell Colette, she'd charge me for the air.
en.Toujours ? Comme ça, droit dans les yeux: Always? Just like that, straight in the eye? I'm impressed. Won't you give me lessons? I'll pay in fruit punch.
en.Tous les matins, je lui pose une seule q: Every morning, I ask him just one question, and I write his answer in my journal. “Your favourite colour?” “Grey.” “Do you have a brother?” “No.” “Do you like dark tonic?” “Yes.” One day, I asked him if he was afraid of anything. He looked at me for a long time and said: “Next.” I wrote down “Next”. It counts.
en.Tout le monde croit que je parle aux cro: Everyone thinks I talk to crocodiles to calm them down. I'll tell you the truth, {surnom}. I talk to them because I'm scared. When I talk, my legs stop shaking. So I tell them about my day, the barley, the barley water, the onions. They listen. They don't come closer. Maybe they're bored. That suits me.
en.Trois ans plus tard, on s'est croisés da: Three years later, we crossed paths in the fog off the south point, him in his longboat, me in a rowing boat. We argued over right of way for an hour, at the top of our voices. Then he held out a bottle of dark tonic on the end of a boathook, and I a mug of sparkling apple. Each of us said the other's drink was revolting. We drank the lot.
en.Trois noix de coco, et mon punch revit !: Three coconuts, and my fruit punch lives again! The jungle boat hasn't come by. You can find some at Colette's, or under the coconut palms in the jungle.
en.Trois semaines à quai. La nuit, mes homm: Three weeks at the quay. At night, my men search the caves with lanterns. Mâchefer counts the days until the end of summer, grinding his teeth. In the evening, Mama Lou's dark tonic. By day, the weaver, who's weaving me a carpet… a very special one. Old Fatima, who answers me in riddles. And the caïd, up there, keeping watch on me. By the captain's beard, I'm very well surrounded.
en.Tu as déjà vu de l'eau, ou seulement du: Have you ever seen water, or only dark tonic?
en.Tu essaies. C'est honnête. C'est déjà pl: You're trying. That's honest. That's already more than half my customers. Here, a dark tonic, on the house. To keep you going. Easy, it bites.
en.Un cidre de Montjoie à la Grenouille Rep: A Montjoie sparkling apple at La Grenouille Repue
en.Un grog de soufre au Diable Repu: A hot sulphur punch at the Diable Repu
en.Un grog pour moi, un grog pour toi ! San: A hot honey for me, a hot honey for you! Cheers, and may the sea be gentle with you!
en.Un jour de grand vent, mon pédalo préfér: One very windy day, my favourite pedalo snapped its mooring and headed out to sea, all by itself. The “Gérard”, of course. Kevin dived off the lifeguard station, swam out to it and pushed it back, like a dolphin pushing a ball. The tourists applauded. I bought him fruit punch for a week.
en.Un matin, en ouvrant les volets, j'ai tr: One morning, opening the shutters, I found the cage empty. No more parrot, just a blue feather on the perch. I kept the name, of course: you don't change a sign that cost that much lemonade. I carved a wooden parrot and put it above the counter. I tell everyone it flew away. The other one doesn't talk, but it listens very well.
en.Un matin, il est monté m'offrir une bout: One morning, he came up to offer me a bottle of Mama Lou's dark tonic, “between guardians of the sea”. I took the bottle, uncorked it, and poured it into the sea over the battlements, down to the last drop. He watched. He said: “The fish are going to be in a good mood.” He went back down. He still greets me.
en.Un matin, à l'aube, l'Amiral a réveillé: One morning at dawn, the Admiral woke the whole Fondouk squawking “DARK TONIC! DARK TONIC! DARK TONIC!”. The whole courtyard up, and Mbarek on the landing, looking like someone who'd dreamed of a raid. Gaspard came down bright red and paid me for an extra night to apologise. I accepted. On principle.
en.Un punch coco à la paillote: A coconut fruit punch at the beach hut
en.Un punch que tout l'archipel viendrait b: A fruit punch the whole archipelago would come to drink at the Perroquet: the dwarves with their beards in the glass, the elves dipping their lips in it, the folk from under the sea, if there are any. A punch that everyone would agree on.
A fruit punch. Without a ladle in it.
A dark tonic, Mâchefer. Just one.
en.Un soir, Lola a écrit sur l'ardoise : «: One evening, Lola wrote on the chalkboard: “Sweethearts' Fruit Punch”. I didn't even know we had one. She'd doubled the recipe: twice the coconut, twice the sugar. Lucas drank three. He went home singing, the big shy lump. I didn't say a thing. I left the line on the board. It's still there.
en.Un soir, Lucas est entré pendant que je: One evening, Lucas came in just as I was bringing Django his fruit punch. Django saw and slowed his waltz down. So much that I had to cross the Perroquet in slow motion, in time with the music, with my tray, like in a dream. The whole room was watching me. Lucas too. I've never walked so slowly in my life.
en.Un soir, deux marins de passage ont sort: One evening, two passing sailors drew their knives at my table. I snapped my fingers, and my two friends stood up. Monsieur Crochet stood up too, without my asking, and laid his hook on the table, in plain view. The knives went back into pockets. I offered him a dark tonic. He didn't say thank you. He didn't need to.
en.Un soir, deux marins de passage ont voul: One evening, two passing sailors wanted to fight at his table, with knives. Sylvain snapped his fingers. His two big lads stood up. So did I. The Code says: fists, never blades. The sailors looked at my hook, then at the lads, then at the door. They chose the door. Sylvain bought me a dark tonic. No questions.
en.Un soir, elle m'a regardé boire mon rhum: One evening she watched me drink my dark tonic. A long time. Then she said my age. Right. And the name of my first captain. Right too. I'd told nobody here. She said: “I know sailors who drink like you.” Hm. I'm wary now. I drink the same way.
en.Un soir, il a joué un air avec de grands: One evening, he played a tune with big drumbeats, BOOM, BOOM, like my cannons. I heard it! All of it! I tapped my foot. Mama Grog says I almost smiled. That's not true. I clenched my teeth so as not to smile. IT'S NOT THE SAME. But I bought him a hot honey, the fiddler. For the drum.
en.Un soir, il m'a apporté une perche contr: One evening, he brought me a perch in exchange for a jar of barley water. The perch leapt out of the basket, straight into my dough. It swam in it, I swear, like in the river! Khéty fell off the bench laughing. I baked the dough anyway: “perch bread”, a hit. I never made it again. You can't find perch that motivated any more.
en.Un soir, j'ai joué un air de marins avec: One evening, I played a sailors' tune with a drum, really whacking it: BOOM, BOOM. Belle-Humeur, in the corner by the fireplace, tapped his foot. His moustache twitched. Mama Grog swears he smiled. He swears he didn't. Afterwards, he bought me a hot honey without a word. For a man who shouts everything, that was a speech.
en.Un soir, je lui ai échangé une perche co: One evening, I traded her a perch for a jar of barley water. The perch wasn't quite dead. It leapt out of the basket, straight into the bread dough. Mérit screamed, the perch swam in the dough, and I laughed until I fell off the bench. The next day, Mérit was selling “perch bread”. It sold out in an hour.
en.Un soir, la bonde d'une barrique de cidr: One evening, the bung of a sparkling-apple barrel got stuck, and Tonneau was looking at me with puppy-dog eyes. I threw a knife from the back of the room: the bung popped out, straight into his glass. Tonneau clapped as if I'd saved the world, and fell off his stool. Mama Grog made me pay for the stool.

One evening, the bung of a sparkling-apple cask was stuck. I tried with my fingers, with a spoon, with my teeth. Nothing. Scarlett threw a knife from the back of the room: pop! The bung flew out, straight into my glass. I clapped so hard I fell off my stool. It was the most beautiful thing I've ever seen. Hic!
en.Un soir, pour voir, je lui ai servi un v: One evening, just to see, I served him a glass of water. Well water, in a dark-tonic glass. He downed it in one, pulled a face, and said: “Strong, but good!” I laughed so hard two pirates fell off their stools. I never told him. He thinks he's getting used to it.
en.Un soir, pêcheurs et pirates allaient se: One evening, fishermen and pirates were about to come to blows on the quay over a net. Hassan arrived with his teapot, me with my dark tonic. He served on the left, I served on the right. An hour later, everyone was singing. He says it was his tea. Ha! I saw the pirates pour dark tonic into his tea. So it was my dark tonic.

One evening, fishermen and pirates were about to fight on the quay, over a net. Mama Lou came out with her dark tonic, me with my tea. She served on one side, I served on the other. An hour later, everyone was singing. She says it was the dark tonic. I say it was the tea. Both sides drank both. That proves nothing.
en.Un tiers de parchemin jauni, déchiré en: A third of a yellowed parchment, torn in a zigzag, covered in dotted lines, arrows and dark-tonic stains: a piece of Barbe-Sanglante's map.
en.Un touriste de l'espace ? Vert ? Gélatin: A space tourist? Green? Jelly-like? (She bursts out laughing.) He can come in for a hot honey, he won't be the weirdest one in the room! Right, the photo. Hold on. (She spits in her hand, smooths her hair, strikes a pose with her fists on her hips.) Like this. With the Crâne Fendu behind me. So everyone can see it's a respectable tavern. Click! … I look small in there. And all shiny. I like it. Tell your jelly we pay BEFORE we brawl.
en.Un vieux parchemin taché de rhum : une c: An old parchment stained with dark tonic: a coastline, dotted lines, a red cross. Captain Salazar Croc-de-Sel cares about it more than his wooden leg.
en.Un vrai ! Punch du héros pour le héros !: A real one! Hero's fruit punch for the hero!
en.Une fois, après deux bières, j'ai avoué: Once, after two jars of barley water, I confessed to Mérit that I loved someone. That very evening, all of Per-Hâpy knew, even the crocodiles. Luckily, I hadn't told her who. She's still looking. She's suspected the whole village, even the cacao seller from Yaxché. I say nothing. I smile. It drives her mad.
en.Une fois, pour faire la paix, elle m'a f: Once, to make peace, she had me taste one of her hot honeys. One sip. I coughed for an hour, on the terrace, in front of the caravan drivers. Rabia patted my back until evening. The next day, I brought her a mint tea. She sniffed it and said: “Smells like a garden.” She didn't drink it. We're even.
en.Une fois, pour faire la paix, je lui ai: Once, to make peace, I had him taste a hot honey. The little one, the rainy-day one. One sip. He coughed for an hour on his terrace, red as a lantern. His wife was patting him on the back. He told me it was poison. Where I come from, that's a compliment.
en.Une grande table au milieu du pont, avec: A big table in the middle of the deck, with Mange-Clous's stew, Mama's hot honey, and the whole crew around it. And nobody getting up before the pot's empty. Nobody!
en.Une jarre de bière d'orge, chez Mérit: A jar of barley water, at Mérit's
en.Une lettre ? Pour moi ? (Il l'ouvre avec: A letter? For me? (He opens it with a butter knife.) My cousin from Vulcanie is coming for the Night of Lanterns! She eats enough for four. I'll need more hot honey.
en.Une paillote sur chaque île ! Une chez l: A beach hut on every island! One with the elves, one on the flying island, one under the sea with very long straws. And with the dwarves. Especially with the dwarves: they're thirsty, and they don't know coconut fruit punch yet.
en.Une tisane, Sébastien. Dans ton grog, si: An herbal tea, Sébastien. In your hot honey, if you like.
en.Une vraie boutique, avec un toit ! Des f: A real shop, with a roof! Fruit from all over the island: dates from Tazira, juicy apples from Carène… and a till full of jingling coins. Ding!
Hot honey it is. Just a drop.
en.Va, va. Je te réveille pour le grog du s: Off you go, off you go. I'll wake you for the evening hot honey.
en.Vieux. Mais content. Tant qu'il y a du r: Old. But happy. As long as there's dark tonic and someone to listen, Silas is happy.
en.Voir Croc ouvrir ce coffre. Le voir comp: To see Croc open that chest. To see him finally understand what his grandfather left here. That day, I'll stand him a dark tonic. The good one, from the back.
en.Yum Kab m'apporte le miel du balché, la: Yum Kab brings me the honey for the honey water, the festival drink, and the wax for the offerings. He's the only man in Yaxché who makes me laugh during a ceremony. I don't know whether I should thank him for it.
en.Yum Kab. Le miel du balché est prêt ?: Yum Kab. Is the honey for the honey water ready?
en.{surnom} ! Ta place t'attend ! Un grog d: {surnom}! Your seat's waiting! A hot sulphur punch? Nothing but good stuff: sulphur, honey and fire cinnamon. It warms you up without making your head spin.
en.À douze ans, j'ai fait ma première bière: At twelve, I made my first barley water all by myself: half-baked barley loaves crumbled into water, dates for sweetness, and patience. I forgot the patience. My barley water was so sour that even the flies wouldn't touch it. My father took a sip, smiled and said: “Tomorrow, you start again.” I've been starting again for thirty years.
en.Écoute, {surnom}, et que ça reste entre: Listen, {surnom}, and keep this between us. I can't swim. A Kerhervé, admiral of Carène, who sinks like an anvil. The morning I went to parley with Croc-de-Sel, under my coat I had a belt of sparkling-apple corks, sewn the night before. My hands were shaking. He thought it was anger.
en.… (Gaspard sourit. Le perroquet : « TOUT: … (Gaspard smiles. The parrot: “ALL GOOD! ALL GOOD! DARK TONIC!”)

es.(Jambe-de-Bois se frotte la mâchoire.) T: (Jambe-de-Bois se frota la mandíbula.) Pegas fuerte, para ser de tierra firme. Toma la bolsa. Cuarenta monedas. Dile a Mama que es la última vez. … Y que su miel caliente sigue siendo la mejor.
es.(Tu voulais dire %s… mais le grog a parl: (Querías decir %s… pero se te trabó la lengua: %s)
(Querías decir %s… pero se te trabó la lengua: %s)
es.Ah ! Le parfum ! Tiens, trois punchs, et: ¡Ah! ¡Qué aroma! Toma, tres ponches de frutas y unas monedas. En el Perroquet estás en tu casa.
es.Ah, {surnom} ! Ta place est chaude. Un g: ¡Ah, {surnom}! Tu sitio sigue caliente. ¿Una miel caliente?
es.Aloha ! Bienvenue au Coco Loco ! Cocktai: ¡Aloha! ¡Bienvenido al Coco Loco! Ponche de frutas, sombra y mala música de regalo.
es.Amenemhat boit sa bière en lisant, il en: Amenemhat se bebe el agua de cebada leyendo, la derrama sobre sus papiros, y cuenta una historia en cada trago. Siempre paga. Con retraso, y con un poema.
es.Amenemhat boit sa bière en lisant. Il re: Amenemhat se bebe el agua de cebada mientras lee. Siempre derrama un poco sobre el papiro. Sus papiros huelen a cebada.
es.Après l'histoire de la soupe, elle a aff: Después del asunto de la sopa, colgó en la puerta de su cocina: « Prohibido el paso a los peces globo », con un pez tachado. Todo el puerto se rio. Yo también, al principio. Pero al día siguiente me trajo una miel caliente sin decir nada, porque todos se burlaban de mí. Ella es así. Picante y dulce.
es.Après l'histoire de sa soupe, tout le po: Después de lo de su sopa, todo el puerto se burlaba de él. Colgué en la puerta de mi cocina: « Prohibido el paso a los peces globo », con un pez tachado, para que todo el mundo se riera del cartel y no de él. Luego le llevé una miel caliente. Me miró con ojos de perro mojado. Nunca volvimos a hablar de ello.
es.Assieds-toi. Serre les dents. … Voilà. T: Siéntate. Aprieta los dientes. … Ya está. Tres puntos de sutura, un poco de bálsamo y un sorbito de tónico oscuro (para mí). Estás como nuevo. Bueno, como de segunda mano.
es.Au Crâne Fendu, le grog est chaud et les: En el Crâne Fendu, la miel está caliente y los puños también. En el Diente del Tiburón, pierdes las monedas. Yo hago las dos cosas, así vuelvo a casa ligerito.
es.Au troisième étage du donjon, il y a tre: En el tercer piso de la mazmorra, hace treinta años, me entró el pánico delante de una rana y volví a subir corriendo. Odon me esperó abajo dos horas, con el almuerzo. Cuando volví a bajar, rojo como un tomate, me tendió una tostada sin decir palabra. Desde entonces, cada año, ese día, nos comemos una tostada juntos. Y yo pago la manzana espumosa.
es.Aujourd'hui, L'Alambic tourne bien. Je v: Hoy, L'Alambic va bien. Vendo mis pociones a los maestros cansados y mis jarabes a los aprendices. Compro las hierbas de Mère Sauge y la miel de Berthe, y Mirabelle ocupa mi sótano. Por la noche, voy a probar las pociones del día al Caldero, con una bebida de miel para enjuagar. Vuelvo a casa cantando. Desafinado, por lo visto. Yo no me oigo.
es.Aujourd'hui, j'ai l'étal des armes au Gr: Hoy tengo el puesto de armas del Gran Mercado. Ferronde forja, yo vendo, discutimos los precios los viernes. Pyrus regatea para la Guardia. Y al lado, Zébuline y sus especias. No tengo nada contra las especias. Mi nariz, sí. Por la noche, bebo un ponche caliente de azufre en el Diable Repu. Sin especias. Lo pedí.
es.Aujourd'hui, j'ai la terrasse du Fondouk: Hoy tengo la terraza del Fondouk. Moulay Brahim y sus partidas de damas, en las que hace trampa; Zineb y sus carteles; Mama Lou, en su taberna, que dice que su tónico oscuro hace la paz mejor que mi té. Y el cocinero de los piratas, que llega cada día con su saquito de sal. Escondo el salero. Al resto de Tazira lo sirvo, y vuelve.
es.Aujourd'hui, j'ai trente ruches. Je vend: Hoy tengo treinta colmenas. Vendo la miel en el mercado del maíz, más barata de lo que querría Ix Chab. Le llevo la miel para el agua de miel a Ix Kanul. Por la tarde juego a las tabas con Ah Kin Pech, que hace trampas al contar. Balam me encuentra colmenas salvajes, y el pequeño Kinich viene a lamer la cuchara. Una vida dulce. Como debe ser.
es.Aujourd'hui, j'enseigne aux enfants du v: Hoy enseño a los niños del pueblo los signos, las cuentas y los buenos modales de Thot. A mediodía, bebo el agua de cebada de Mérit releyendo mis papiros. Mis alumnos me llaman el hipopótamo, por mis siestas. Creen que no lo sé. Pero Tueris, la diosa hipopótamo, protege a los niños. Así que me lo tomo como un título. Bien merecido.
es.Aujourd'hui, j'ouvre à dix heures et je: Hoy abro a las diez y cierro a la una de la madrugada. Django en el escenario, Lola entre las mesas, Hector al final de la barra, el Lord que paga en oro, y Kiki, mi rival del ponche de frutas, que viene a tomar algo a mi casa después de cerrar la suya. Y un misterio: el barco de la jungla ya no para en mi casa. Raro, ¿eh?
es.Aujourd'hui, je pêche au bout du ponton,: Hoy, pesco al final del embarcadero, paso a los pocos visitantes y conozco cada corriente de la isla por su nombre de pila. A mediodía, una bebida de miel en casa de Berthe; por la noche, mi mesa y mi trozo de tarta. Una vez al año, llevo a Borée a dar la vuelta a la isla. El embarcadero lo alargué con las escaleras de Théophraste. No preguntes.
es.Aujourd'hui, je tiens le Diable Repu. On: Hoy llevo el Diable Repu. Servimos ponche caliente de azufre, sin una gota de azufre de verdad, café del Brasier y mi lava helada. El capitán cuenta su tormenta, Kraxx estornuda, Moloka se ríe, y Bobor viene a « desempatar » nuestros postres. Por la noche, es el ruido más bonito del mundo.
es.Aujourd'hui, je travaille sur le Sans-Pi: Hoy trabajo en el Despiadado de la mañana a la noche. Cuarenta tablas cambiadas, todo el costado calafateado, la quilla otra vez a plomo. Coquille viene a cantar mientras clavo, Brutus me forja los herrajes y el Viejo Silas me cuenta historias de barcos junto a la hoguera de la playa. Por la noche, una manzana espumosa en el Crâne Fendu. La manzana espumosa de Carène. Casi como en casa.
Hoy, el Campo de Duelos es mío. Cinco braseros, tres maniquíes de paja, aprendices con las cejas chamuscadas, y Oscar. A mediodía como en casa de Berthe; por la noche me tomo allí un tónico oscuro de la Murène, cuando Mathurin me ha dejado. Grito mucho. Enseño a los jóvenes a apagar lo que encienden. Es lo más difícil. Nadie quiere aprender eso.
es.Aujourd'hui, la Veuve est amarrée au pon: Hoy, la Viuda está amarrada en el pantalán este. Scarlett lleva la tripulación, el Mudo lleva las velas, Tonneau lleva la barra. Por la noche, juego en la mesa grande del Diente del Tiburón. Pierdo más de lo que gano. Y está ese asunto de las cuarenta monedas con Mama Grog. Una cuestión de principios: su miel caliente de aquel martes estaba tibia. Ella dice que no.
es.Aujourd'hui, ma boutique est ouverte de: Hoy, mi tienda abre de nueve de la mañana a ocho de la tarde. Compro de todo: perlas, rubíes, dientes de cocodrilo, esquirlas de cristal, conchas. Vendo un poco de todo: tónico oscuro, llavecitas y dados que ruedan… mejor. Sylvain me los compra todos los meses para tirarlos al mar. El negocio va bien. El negocio siempre va bien. Yo cuento.
es.Autrefois la cloche réglait toute la vie: Antes la campana regía toda la vida de la ciudad: el mercado a las ocho, la siesta a la una, la petanca a las siete. Sobre todo la petanca.
es.Avec du RHUM ? Sacrilège ! Tu as passé t: ¿Con TÓNICO OSCURO? ¡Sacrilegio! Has pasado demasiado tiempo con los piratas. … Te lo sirvo igualmente. Sin tónico oscuro. Y te lo beberás, y ya verás.
Con un poco de tónico oscuro.
es.Berthe ! Deux pots de miel, et un hydrom: ¡Berthe! Dos tarros de miel y una bebida de miel.
es.Bienvenue à la Chope Ardente ! La seule: ¡Bienvenido a la Jarra Ardiente! La única taberna bajo un volcán. Ulfa Chope-Pleine. ¿Un burbujeante? ¿Dos? ¿El barril entero?
es.Bienvenue, bienvenue ! Mérit. Le pain, c: ¡Bienvenido, bienvenido! Mérit. El pan soy yo; el agua de cebada soy yo; los chismes también. ¿Pan calentito? Acaba de salir del horno.
es.C'est le Capitaine qui nous a mariés, Mo: Fue el capitán quien nos casó, a Moloka y a mí, en su muelle. Dio un discurso de una hora sobre el mar y las sardinas. Lloré tanto que mojé la sardina enmarcada. Desde entonces, en nuestro aniversario, le invito a su ponche caliente, y él cuenta nuestra propia boda. También le añade olas.
es.C'est lui qui a fait ma grande jarre à b: Él me hizo la gran jarra de agua de cebada. Le dije que se inclinaba un poco a la izquierda. Volvió con una plomada, midió tres veces y dijo: « La jarra está recta. La que se inclina eres tú. » Me reí tanto que le derramé un cucharón de agua de cebada en las sandalias. Se enfurruñó. Volvió esa misma noche.
es.Capitaine ! Ta table est prête. Et ton g: ¡Capitán! Tu mesa está lista. ¡Y tu ponche caliente!
es.Celui-là a des rimes, Mérit. Il vaut deu: Este rima, Mérit. Vale dos aguas de cebada.
es.Cette année, c'est sûr. Au troisième cid: Este año, seguro. A la tercera manzana espumosa fijamos la fecha.
es.Cette île est la plus grande de l'archip: Esta isla es la más grande del archipiélago. Mi abuelo decía que tenía un corazón de piedra, y que ese corazón valía más que todos los tesoros del mundo. Decía muchas cosas, después del tónico oscuro.
es.Chaque année, le jour anniversaire de mo: Cada año, el día del aniversario de mi llegada, le llevo un ponche de frutas a Léon a bordo de la Golondrina. Nos lo tomamos en cubierta, sin hablar, mirando el pueblo al otro lado. Él me enseña mi billete de vuelta, siempre metido en su brújula. Yo le digo: « Guárdalo un poco más. » Ya van cinco ponches de frutas.
es.Chaque année, à la fin de la saison, Hec: Cada año, al final de la temporada, Hector y yo volvemos a hacer la cuenta del letrero en una esquina de la barra: cuántas limonadas, cuántas noches, cuántas jarras. Está pagado desde hace doce años. Cada año miramos el resultado, nos miramos y nos callamos. Le sirvo una limonada. «A cuenta del letrero».
es.Chaque matin, je descends au Cénote pour: Cada mañana, bajo al Cenote para las ofrendas. Luego rezo en lo alto de Kukulkan, velo por la estela con Ah Kin Pech, y por la noche subo a la plataforma de Venus. El pequeño Kinich me sigue con sus preguntas, Chak presume de enfrentarse a Xibalba, y Yum Kab me trae la miel para el agua de miel. La Serpiente Emplumada tiene mucho que hacer. Yo también.
es.Chaque matin, quand je passe sous la Ska: Cada mañana, cuando paso bajo la Skala, me quito el tricornio y hago una reverencia hasta el suelo: « ¡Muy buenos días, caíd! » Él aprieta los dientes. Un día le subí una botella del tónico oscuro de Mama Lou, « entre guardianes del mar ». La vació en el mar delante de mí. Le dije: « Los peces van a estar de buen humor. » Lo sigo saludando. Más bajo.
es.Chaque midi, Brindille se pose sur le re: Cada mediodía, Brindille se posa en el alféizar de mi ventana, pide un café del Brasier y me cuenta todas las noticias de la ciudad en un minuto. Yo le pago con el café; ella me paga con las noticias. Por la noche, se las cuento a los marineros. Hurla dice que es ella quien da las noticias. Yo las sirvo con el ponche caliente.
es.Chaque midi, je raconte à Grumbald toute: Cada mediodía le cuento a Grumbald todas las noticias de la ciudad, en un minuto, entre dos sorbos de café. Por la noche, él se las cuenta a los marineros con el ponche caliente. Un día le conté una noticia inventada, para ver qué pasaba. Por la noche, toda la taberna la conocía. Al día siguiente, Hurla la gritaba en la plaza. Nunca más he mentido.
es.Chaque soir, je garde un punch de côté,: Cada noche guardo un ponche de frutas aparte, detrás de la caja, fresquito. Para Lucas, cuando llega. Toni lo ve. Lo ve todas las noches. Hace como si nada y sirve a los demás silbando. Una vez, sin darse la vuelta, solo dijo: « Tu ponche secreto estaría mejor con pajita. »
es.Charming little town ! Le thé est épouva: Charming little town! El té es espantoso, pero el ponche de frutas del Perroquet es divino.
es.Chez Berthe, il n'arrive qu'une bouteill: A casa de Berthe solo llega una botella de tónico oscuro de la Murène al mes. Mathurin la quiere, yo también. Una noche nos la jugamos: si veía una serpiente antes de medianoche, era suya. A las doce menos cuarto vio tres. Eran algas. Nos la bebimos juntos, para no enfadarnos.
es.Dans ma famille, on fait du pain depuis: En mi familia, hacemos pan desde la pirámide. Una tatarabuela mía daba de comer a los obreros de la meseta. De pequeña, pisaba la masa de cebada con los pies, en la gran tina, cantando. Mi madre decía que el agua de cebada salía mejor cuando cantaba afinada. Esos años salió mala muchas veces.
es.Dans un grog, Doc ! Dans un grog !: ¡En una miel caliente, Doc! ¡En una miel caliente!
es.De neuf heures à dix-neuf heures, je sui: De nueve de la mañana a siete de la tarde, estoy en mi silla. Quinientas flexiones entre pitido y pitido. Rescato a los clientes de Yannick, vigilo mi desafío de las estrellas de mar, mi madre me grita que vaya a ayudarla. Por la noche, ponche de frutas en el chiringuito de Kiki con Yannick. Luego vuelvo a la calle del Faro, donde mi vecino el sargento me saluda con mucha educación. Demasiada.
es.Depuis des années, Salomé veut le trente: Desde hace años, Salomé quiere el trigésimo tercer ingrediente de mi ras el hanout. Me lo ha ofrecido todo, por caravana y por Zéphyr: cuerdas, faroles, un tonel de manzana espumosa y una vez, su propio sombrero. Me quedé el sombrero. No le di el secreto. Ella lo sigue intentando. Es una auténtica comerciante.
es.Depuis la nuit où il est tombé du quai,: Desde la noche que se cayó del muelle, le sirvo una miel caliente especial: limón caliente, miel, canela y una lágrima de tónico oscuro. Una lagrimita de nada. Nunca se ha dado cuenta. Dice que es la mejor miel caliente del mundo. Mejor. El Doc dice que así vivirá cien años. Yo quiero que viva cien años.
es.Deux punchs et une bière naine, table tr: ¡Dos ponches de frutas y un burbujeante enano, mesa tres!
es.Doc ! Un grog, et ma fièvre f'envole !: ¡Doc! ¡Una miel caliente, y mi fiebre ze va volando!
es.Doc Faignée cherche des herbes du marais: Doc Faignée bufca hierbaf del pantano para curar la fiebre. Yo digo que una buena miel caliente lo cura todo.
es.Doc Faignée veut toufours me foigner. Mo: Doc Zaignée ziempre quiere curarme. Yo digo que una buena miel caliente lo cura todo. Él dice que no. Noz puzimoz de acuerdo: él echa zu infuzión en mi miel caliente. Azí, loz doz tenemoz razón.
es.Du jus de coco ! Hic ! C'est bon, ça ! L: ¡Zumo de coco! ¡Hip! ¡Eso está bueno! El capitán odia el ponche de frutas con coco, dice que sabe a playa. A mí me gusta la playa.
es.Elle a dit que ma grande jarre à bière p: Dijo que mi gran jarra de agua de cebada estaba torcida. ¡Una jarra mía! Cogí mi plomada y medí tres veces. Recta como una columna. Le dije: « La que está torcida eres tú. » Se rio y me derramó agua de cebada en las sandalias. Me enfurruñé. Volví por la tarde. Por la jarra. Evidentemente.
es.Elle m'a demandé d'aller couper des arbr: Me pidió que fuera a talar árboles a la selva, para sus mástiles. Demasiadas arañas. Le dije que no. Me dijo: « ¿Tú, miedo de una araña? » Le dije: « Sí. » Se rio. Luego dijo: « Yo también. » Nos tomamos una manzana espumosa. Seguimos sin mástil. Tenemos un amigo más.
es.Elle m'a donné de l'hibiscus séché pour: Me dio hibisco seco para sustituir el coral. En el cuenco, un rojo sublime, profundo, casi color zumo de uva.
